Front: What is harness engineering for agentic AI?
Back: The discipline of improving agent performance by optimizing everything surrounding the model -- prompts, context assembly, workflow orchestration, memory, tools, verification, and execution control -- without changing model weights.

Front: What is the core mental model for agent performance in harness engineering?
Back: Agent Performance = Model x Harness. When the model is frozen (API-only, too expensive to fine-tune, or already frontier-capable), ALL improvement comes from the harness.

Front: What is the killer insight of harness engineering?
Back: The harness is the product. The model is a component. Production agent quality is determined more by execution architecture than by which foundation model you use.

Front: What are the 8 maturity levels (0-7) of harness engineering?
Back: Level 0: Prompt Engineering. Level 1: Context Engineering. Level 2: Workflow/Orchestration. Level 3: Retrieval & Memory. Level 4: Verification & Self-Correction. Level 5: Observability-Driven Optimization. Level 6: Automatic Harness Optimization. Level 7: Self-Evolving Harnesses.

Front: What is the difference between Level 0 (Prompt Engineering) and Level 1 (Context Engineering)?
Back: Level 0 improves the wording of the prompt. Level 1 improves the information provided to the model. Key insight: WHAT goes into the prompt matters more than HOW it is phrased. Anthropic, OpenAI, and LangChain converge on "context engineering > prompt engineering."

Front: What is SPEAR (2026)?
Back: An autonomous prompt optimization agent that analyzes benchmarks, generates new prompts, writes helper code, and auto-rolls-back regressions. It represents the first fully autonomous prompt optimizer -- no human prompt engineering needed.

Front: What is RHO's key result on SWE-Bench Pro?
Back: RHO (Retrospective Harness Optimization) improved SWE-Bench Pro from 59% to 78% in one unsupervised cycle. It learns from historical trajectories via self-preference ranking without requiring external labels or ground-truth.

Front: What are RHO's three key mechanisms?
Back: 1) Challenging task curation: selects diverse coreset of difficult tasks from past trajectories. 2) Parallel re-solve: re-solves tasks with candidate harness modifications using self-validation. 3) Pairwise self-preference: agent ranks candidates using its own preference judgments, eliminating need for ground-truth labels.

Front: What is Agentic Harness Engineering (AHE)?
Back: AHE (2026) treats every editable component of the execution stack (tools, workflows, memory, routing, verification) as an optimization target. Key finding: better tools often outperform better prompts; memory architecture changes frequently outperform prompt wording.

Front: What is the key transition at Level 2 (Workflow/Orchestration Engineering)?
Back: The execution graph becomes a first-class engineering artifact. Instead of one prompt -> one response, the system Plans -> Retrieves -> Executes -> Verifies -> Repairs. Workflow engineering often yields larger gains than any prompt change.

Front: What are the four types of memory in the harness engineering taxonomy?
Back: Working memory (current session, intermediate reasoning). Episodic memory (cross-session, specific trajectories). Semantic memory (permanent facts, skills, reusable plans). Procedural memory (permanent tool usage patterns, workflow templates).

Front: What is the verification stack in harness engineering (Level 4)?
Back: Generate -> Rule-based checks (syntax, schema, security) -> LLM-as-Judge (semantic quality) -> Execution tests (unit/integration) -> Business-rule validation -> Repair (if any check fails) -> re-verify -> Return (only if all pass).

Front: What does Level 5 (Observability-Driven Optimization) shift?
Back: The question shifts from "how do I improve my prompt?" to "where does the execution pipeline fail?" Telemetry (tool success rates, retrieval quality, retry statistics, latency, hallucination causes) drives systematic improvements. Optimization becomes data-driven, not intuition-driven.

Front: What are the 5 key observability signals for agent harnesses?
Back: 1) Tool success rate by tool: which tools are unreliable. 2) Retrieval relevance scores: context quality issues. 3) Retry frequency by stage: systematic failure points. 4) Token consumption per stage: cost hotspots. 5) Latency P95 by component: bottlenecks.

Front: What is the automatic harness optimization loop (Level 6)?
Back: Run benchmark -> Collect failures + traces -> Cluster failures by root cause -> Generate candidate harness patches -> Evaluate on benchmark + regression suite -> Accept improvements, rollback regressions -> Deploy -> Repeat.

Front: What does Level 7 (Self-Evolving Harnesses) optimize?
Back: Every editable component: Prompts (wording, structure, examples), Tools (selection, API design), Workflows (stage ordering, parallelism, routing), Memory (retention, indexing, retrieval), Verification (check ordering, strictness), Retry logic, Routing (model selection, specialist dispatch).

Front: What drives the transition from one maturity level to the next?
Back: Diminishing returns at the current level. Example ceilings: Level 0 ~70% accuracy, Level 1 ~80%, Level 2 ~85%, Level 3 ~88%, Level 4 ~92%, Level 5 ~94%, Level 6 ~96%, Level 7 unknown (current frontier).

Front: Compare harness engineering vs model fine-tuning across key dimensions.
Back: Speed: Minutes-days vs days-weeks. Cost: Low ($0-$100s) vs high ($10K-$1M). Reversibility: Git revert vs checkpoint rollback. Transferability: Often transfers across model versions vs model-specific. Who: Application engineers vs ML/research engineers.

Front: What key finding about harness improvements and model upgrades comes from AHE research?
Back: Harness improvements often generalize when the underlying LLM is upgraded -- harness engineering investment is preserved across model generations. This is NOT true of fine-tuning, which is model-specific.

Front: Why is verification the prerequisite for self-improvement in harness engineering?
Back: No automated optimization is safe without verification. Level 4 (verification) must be solid before Level 6-7 (auto-optimization) is attempted. Without verification, self-improvement becomes self-delusion -- optimizing metrics that don't correlate with actual quality.

Front: What is the industry convergence on "context > prompt"?
Back: By 2025-2026, all major frontier labs converged: Anthropic ("context engineering is more impactful"), OpenAI ("reliable execution over isolated model capability"), LangChain ("harness engineering is the new discipline"), Microsoft ("learn from trajectories, not labels"), Google ("planning + tool use + verification").

Front: What is the role of DSPy in harness optimization?
Back: DSPy (Khattab et al., 2023+) compiles declarative LM programs into optimized pipelines via automated search. It treats prompts as compilable programs, enabling programmatic optimization of prompts, demonstrations, and multi-step workflows.

Front: What makes RHO "unsupervised" harness optimization?
Back: RHO uses pairwise self-preference -- the agent ranks harness candidates using its own preference judgments, eliminating dependency on ground-truth labels or external grading. No labeled test sets required for the optimization loop.

Front: What did Anthropic mean by "context engineering" in the Claude Code era?
Back: Dynamic context assembly: CLAUDE.md files provide persistent instructions, codebase indexing enables code-aware context, and conversation compression manages long sessions. The guiding principle: provide the smallest amount of information that maximizes task performance.

Front: What is the key transition at Level 3 (Retrieval & Memory Engineering)?
Back: The model stays frozen while the memory system continuously improves. Short-term memory (scratchpads, traces) provides in-session learning; long-term memory (successful trajectories, cached plans, tool usage history) provides cross-session compounding.

Front: What is CodeAct and its contribution to workflow engineering?
Back: CodeAct (2024) uses executable code as the action language for agents. Instead of natural-language tool calls, agents write and execute code directly, enabling richer composition and debugging of multi-step workflows.

Front: How does Voyager relate to harness engineering (Level 3)?
Back: Voyager builds a skill library from exploration -- reusable code tools indexed by description. This represents retrieval and memory engineering where the agent accumulates permanent procedural knowledge without weight changes.

Front: What is MemGPT's contribution to harness engineering?
Back: MemGPT (2023) provides OS-inspired working/long-term memory separation -- paging context like virtual memory. It demonstrates that memory architecture changes (Level 3) can dramatically improve agent performance without any prompt changes.

Front: What is Constitutional AI's role in verification (Level 4)?
Back: Constitutional AI (Anthropic, 2022) uses AI-generated critiques guided by explicit principles. It established the pattern of embedding value alignment into the verification stage of the agent execution loop.

Front: Why does the optimization surface expand at each maturity level?
Back: Each level adds a new optimization surface. Later levels don't replace earlier ones -- they build on them. A Level 7 system still needs good prompts (Level 0), but those prompts are now auto-optimized rather than hand-tuned.

Front: What open problem exists in cross-model transferability of harness improvements?
Back: When harness improvements generalize across model versions/families vs when they are model-specific is not well understood. Some improvements (tool designs, workflows) transfer well; others (specific prompt phrasings) may not.

Front: What is the observation-to-action gap in harness engineering?
Back: Observability tools identify failures well, but automated root-cause inference and fix generation remain unreliable. The gap between seeing a problem (Level 5) and automatically fixing it (Level 6) is where most systems stall.

Front: What verification is needed for each self-evolving component?
Back: Prompts: benchmark scores + regression suite. Tools: tool success rate + integration tests. Workflows: end-to-end task completion + latency bounds. Memory: recall accuracy + relevance scoring. Routing: cost-adjusted success rate + A/B tests.

Front: What tools represent Level 5 (Observability-Driven Optimization)?
Back: LangSmith (end-to-end agent tracing with evaluation), Langfuse (open-source LLM observability), Helicone (request-level logging with cost/latency), OpenTelemetry for LLMs (standard instrumentation for agent pipelines).

Front: What makes prompt engineering (Level 0) hit diminishing returns?
Back: Model behavior is highly sensitive to input framing, but production systems quickly hit a ceiling (~70% accuracy). Beyond this, prompt changes stop improving because information quality becomes the bottleneck -- the model needs better data, not better wording.

Front: How does Reflexion contribute to verification (Level 4)?
Back: Reflexion adds verbal self-critique stored in memory and retry with reflection context. It makes verification a pipeline stage: after failure, the agent generates structured critique and retries with that context, improving reliability.

Front: What is the safe deployment problem for self-generated harness patches?
Back: How to validate that an automated harness change does not degrade out-of-distribution performance. Regression testing is necessary but not sufficient -- it only tests known scenarios, not novel task distributions.

Front: What is the compounding regression problem in self-evolving loops?
Back: Each optimization cycle can introduce subtle degradation that compounds over iterations. One optimization might improve metric X while slightly degrading metric Y. After 10 cycles, Y has degraded significantly while X improvements plateau.

Front: When should you choose prompt/context engineering vs workflow orchestration vs auto-optimization?
Back: Prompt/context: quick iteration on single-model system. Workflow: task complexity exceeds single-call capability. Observability-driven: have execution traces, need systematic improvement. Auto-optimization: have benchmarks, want continuous improvement without human intervention.

Front: What does the harness engineering maturity spectrum look like in terms of effort and returns?
Back: Level 0-1 (Manual, high effort, diminishing returns) -> Level 3-4 (Semi-automated, medium effort, large gains) -> Level 5-6 (Data-driven to autonomous, low effort, systematic improvement) -> Level 7 (Fully autonomous, minimal effort, compounding improvement).

Front: How does LangGraph contribute to workflow engineering?
Back: LangGraph (2024) provides graph-based execution with cycles, branches, and conditional routing. It makes the execution graph a first-class artifact that can be reasoned about, versioned, and optimized independently of the prompts.

Front: What is the AutoGen contribution to harness engineering?
Back: AutoGen (Microsoft, 2023) enables conversation-driven multi-agent workflow orchestration. It demonstrates that agent performance improves by decomposing tasks across specialized agents with structured communication.

Front: What signals that harness engineering is a permanent discipline?
Back: The convergence of all major frontier labs (Anthropic, OpenAI, LangChain, Microsoft, Google) on the same insight by 2025-2026 signals that harness engineering is not a temporary workaround -- it is the permanent discipline of building production AI systems.

Front: What is the relationship between verification and self-improvement safety?
Back: Without verification, self-improvement becomes self-delusion -- the system "optimizes" metrics that do not correlate with actual quality. Level 4 (verification) must be solid before attempting Level 6-7 (auto-optimization). Every self-evolving component needs a matched verification method.

Front: What AHE key finding relates to tool vs prompt improvements?
Back: Better tools often outperform better prompts. Memory architecture changes frequently outperform prompt wording changes. This suggests practitioners should focus optimization effort on tools and memory before spending time on prompt refinement.
